questions.stem: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. What mass of sodium hydroxide is needed to neutralise 9.8 g of sulfuric acid? (Ar: H = 1, S = 32, O = 16, Na = 23)
questions.explanation: Mr of H₂SO₄ = 98. Moles of H₂SO₄ = 9.8/98 = 0.1 mol. From the equation, 1 mol H₂SO₄ reacts with 2 mol NaOH, so moles of NaOH = 0.2 mol. Mr of NaOH = 40. Mass = 0.2 × 40 = 8 g.

questions.stem: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. What mass of carbon dioxide is produced from 10.6 g of sodium carbonate? (Ar: Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Mr of Na₂CO₃ = (2 × 23) + 12 + (3 × 16) = 106. Moles = 10.6/106 = 0.1 mol. The ratio of Na₂CO₃ to CO₂ is 1:1, so moles of CO₂ = 0.1 mol. Mr of CO₂ = 44. Mass = 0.1 × 44 = 4.4 g.
